text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Transhipment company ECT and Danish shipping line Maersk plan jointly to operate a new container terminal in Rotterdam. (p1)
- Transport minister says the major part of the money needed for developing a new Rotterdam port basin should come from private sector. (p1)
- Economic affairs ministry is to launch a special fund for new high-tech companies. (p3)
- Storage and distribution firm Pakhoed upgrades profits forecast. (p3)
- Belgian/Dutch bank insurer Fortis sells Grenswisselkantoren GWK unit to its management and two private investors. (p2)
- Dispensing chemists' cooperative OPG cuts 20 jobs. (p13)
- Pig stock is to be cut by 25 pct in cabinet's bio-industry restructuring plan. (p1)
- Stock brokers on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange hope for a Unilever share split. (p31)
- Builder Ballast Nedam's British unit Wiltshier remains in the red. (p33)
- Retailer Ahold's unit Albert Heijn supermarket chain is the best trendsetter in the Netherlands says small and medium- sized businesses MKB poll. (p1)
- Monopoly position of pilots in Dutch sea ports should end, according to a report presented to ministry of transport.
